candidate.blueprint_locator: Appendix A, printed p. 26, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control → Standard Precautions/Transmission-Based Precautions/Surgical Asepsis: apply infection-prevention principles including hand hygiene.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene
candidate.educational_objective: Perform hand hygiene after contact with equipment or other surfaces in a patient's immediate surroundings, even when the patient was not touched directly.

options.A: Hand hygiene is not required because the nurse did not touch the patient directly.
options.B: Perform hand hygiene after touching equipment in the patient's immediate surroundings, even without direct patient contact.
options.C: Perform hand hygiene after equipment contact only if the device is visibly soiled.
options.D: Defer hand hygiene until the next patient-care task because no blood or body-fluid exposure occurred.

candidate.rationale: CDC healthcare hand-hygiene guidance lists hand hygiene after touching a patient or the patient's surroundings as a clinical indication. CDC Isolation Precautions specifically includes contact with inanimate objects, including medical equipment, in the immediate vicinity of the patient. Therefore, direct patient contact, visible soiling, or blood/body-fluid exposure is not required for this hand-hygiene indication.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC explicitly identifies hand hygiene after touching patient surroundings and after contact with inanimate objects including medical equipment in the patient's immediate vicinity.
candidate.source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
candidate.source_locator: Recommendations → 'Know when to clean your hands' → 'After touching a patient or patient's surroundings'; supporting Isolation Precautions recommendation IV.A.3.e for inanimate objects/medical equipment in the immediate vicinity.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A nurse enters a room, adjusts an IV pump in the patient's immediate surroundings without touching the patient, and then leaves. When is hand hygiene indicated?
